text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index ended at a new record close on Tuesday but fell short of its all-time high as a dithering Dow took the steam out of a strong early rally in British blue-chips. The FTSE closed 50.6 points higher at 4,357.7, just beating the previous closing high set on February 19.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index of top shares closes at record highs, pushed upwards by the strong dollar and rally in the auto sector following bullish noises from a Daimler official on 1996, 1997 results. Dealers wary of some retreat in market ahead of Greenspan testimony on Wednesday. The DAX-30 index of leading shares closed up 56.80 points at 3,320.66, a new record-high. In post-bourse trade the index was up 86.35 at 3,345.09.

PARIS - French shares staged a strong rally on Tuesday, helped by the dollar and bullish underlying sentiment, and closed a whisper away from their all-time high reached on February 18 of this year. The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended up 51.43 points or 1.98 percent at 2,651.69.

ZURICH - Swiss shares firmed more than one percent to end slightly below the day's highs, regaining the 4,500-point level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) after a three-day fall. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 32.45 points, or 1.05 percent, to 2,870.44. TOKYO - Tokyo stocks revived on Tuesday after buy-backs of bank shares resumed and a weaker yen encouraged investors seeking high-technology blue-chip issues. But trade was listless as there was little to steer the market apart from currencices. The 225-share Nikkei average ended the day up 135.65 points or 0.74 percent at 18,564.78.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Tuesday pulled down by investors trimming overweight positions in bank shares. brokers said. "We are seeing some sizeable switching, from the banks into property shares," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia. "Both overseas and local investors were active today." The Hang Seng Index closed 57.20 points lower at 13,450.08.

SYDNEY - Australian shares posted modest gains on Tuesday, the market's rise underpinned by solid gains from a handful of major resources issues boosted by firmer base metal prices. The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 10.9 points firmer at 2,432.4.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares end sharply weaker on a stronger rand and a weaker bullion price which fell below the $360 per ounce level before the close. Industrials ended strong on less than convincing gains in Wall Street overnight. Overall index down 21.2 points to 7,132.6, golds drop 70.0 points or 4.5 pct to 1,492.9 and industrials gain 22.7 points to 8,284.
